cohort: The study included women who gave birth at the Department of Gynecology and Obstetrics of CHU Point G, Bamako, between January 1, 2008, and December 31, 2018, comparing those aged 40 years and above (cases) with those aged 20-34 years (controls).
finding: Pregnancy at 40 years of age and beyond poses a high-risk situation for both mother and child, with advanced maternal age being significantly associated with increased maternal risks such as hypertension, diabetes, placenta previa, and anemia, and newborn risks including stillbirth, prematurity, and macrosomia.
mod_finding: No significant association was found between advanced maternal age and cesarean delivery (OR = 1.22).
